target_customer: University computer science instructors and departments
problem: Grading programming assignments by hand was slow, and students waited long for feedback.
business_model: B2B SaaS per course or institution
product_category: Computer science education platform with autograding

founders.name: Prahasith Veluvolu
education: Purdue University (student at founding, per Purdue release)
founders.background_notes: Founders were Purdue students per IBJ and Purdue

competitors.name: zyBooks (zyLabs)
competitors.what: Auto graded programming labs for intro CS

technical_complexity.rationale: Sandboxed code execution and grading at scale for many languages.

defensibility.rationale: Instructors build assignments into the tool, but competing autograders existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HackerRank, a skills assessment company, acquired Mimir in December 2019, its first acquisition.

market_need_then: Growing CS enrollments strained instructors; Mimir reached 70+ universities by its own claim.

brand_strength.rationale: Name matches Norse figure Mimir but no source ties the choice; little brand coverage beyond local business press.

outcome_analysis: Mimir grew from a Purdue student project to a classroom platform used at 70+ universities with an eight person team, then was bought by HackerRank in December 2019 for an undisclosed price. It was a small niche exit after about $2.5M raised per press, not a venture scale outcome.
notes: Education lines are from the Purdue and IBJ search snippets, not from an opened page; verify. Total raised about $2.5M per IBJ/Purdue snippet; aggregators conflict ($1.5M Employbl; $2.5M seed 2016-12 SeedTable), so seed amount left null. Pre-seed in California 2015 amount unknown. Competitor Gradescope and Codio founding dates not sourced. mimirhq.com returned 503.
